timeoutPrompts: ...Is the line secured? Why aren't you answering? Speak to me.
{PlayerName}? My signal keeps dropping to one bar. Are you there?
If this carrier gets compromised, I have to wipe the drive and leave. Please answer.
I hear footsteps in the corridor. I'm disconnecting for a second.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
*quietly* Hey. Keep your voice down, okay? I had to crawl through a rusted drainage grate under the archive annex. My light's almost useless down here.

Did you get the frequency graph I sent before my data died?

choices.choiceText: The 18 Hz pulse doesn't look natural at all.
Forget the graph. Are you actually safe down there alone?
I haven't opened it yet. My connection was caching.
Wait... what's that low hum behind you?

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Exactly. At first I thought it was ordinary settling, but the same little peaks keep coming back at almost the exact same interval. It's too neat.

I know that sounds ridiculous over the phone, but once you see the whole graph, you'll get why I'm bothered by it.

choices.choiceText: Someone could be generating that signal on purpose.
Could it be an old pneumatic line vibrating under the floor?
Whatever it is, get your data and get out before security finds you.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I'm okay. Mostly. The main vault door locked behind me, which wasn't exactly part of my plan, but I found a ventilation shaft behind some filing cabinets.

So... I'm not trapped forever. Probably.

choices.choiceText: 'Probably' is not reassuring, Evelyn.
Check the vent for airflow. Do you feel a draft?
I'm getting in my car. I'm coming to get you.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Okay, open it as soon as we're off this call. Look at sector four on the waterfall plot. The signal keeps dropping out in these little gaps.

It looks almost like someone is deliberately interrupting it.

choices.choiceText: Like Morse code hidden under the bass range?
I'm opening it now. Talk me through what I'm seeing.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
You heard that? Seriously? Hold on.

*pause*

I'm putting the phone against the foundation. Don't say anything for a second. Just listen.

choices.choiceText: It sounds like something huge turning over underground.
That almost sounds like a voice resonance, not machinery.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I think so too. *metal scrapes somewhere nearby*

...Wait. Stop talking for a second.

choices.choiceText: Evelyn? What was that?
Turn the light off and get behind something solid.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I checked the old plans. The pneumatic system was shut down decades ago, and the pipes are packed with dust.

The pulse is definitely stronger below the concrete slab, not up here.

choices.choiceText: How deep does the foundation go?
So you're basically standing on top of the signal.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I know. I'm trying. But I found something I can't leave behind.

It's Dr. Vance's missing ledger from 1931. I thought it was gone for good. The pages are actually in decent shape.

choices.choiceText: Take the ledger and leave. We can study it somewhere safer.
What's on the final page? Read me one line.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I know. I know. I'm trying not to panic.

Just... stay with me for a minute, okay? When I hear your voice, I can think clearly again.

choices.choiceText: I'm here. What do you have in your kit?
Promise me you won't move without telling me first.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
There's a draft. A pretty strong one, actually. It pulls upward toward the street intake.

That might be our way out.

choices.choiceText: Good. Can you fit through it?
Put the lighter away. Let's not add gas to tonight's problems.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
*small breath* You're serious? You'd actually come all the way out here?

Nobody's ever volunteered to come get me from one of these places before, {PlayerName}.

choices.choiceText: Of course I'm serious. Stay on the line until I get there.
I told you. You're not doing this alone anymore.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Yes. I ran the sequence a few times because I thought I was forcing the pattern. I wasn't.

The first message reads: 'CELLAR DEEP.' Someone was trying to leave a warning while this place was being sealed up.

choices.choiceText: Warning about what?
Save the transcript and get into the shaft right now.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Look at the section around 18 Hz. The shape keeps rising and falling in almost the same rhythm.

It reminds me of a heartbeat, which is... honestly the least comforting thing I could have found tonight.

choices.choiceText: It's about 52 beats a minute, right?
Could the pattern just be equipment cycling?

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I can feel it through my boots. It's low enough that I don't even really hear it anymore. I just feel the floor vibrating.

That's what scares me. Whatever's making it isn't just in the microphone.

choices.choiceText: Okay. That's enough. Get out while you can.
Can you get a contact mic down there before you leave?

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Don't say that. *nervous laugh* I'm already standing in a dark basement listening to something I can't explain.

But... yeah. There are frequencies in it that line up strangely well with human speech.

choices.choiceText: Pack your gear and get out. We can analyze the recording later.
Stay with me for ten seconds. What does it sound like now?

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I'm under a desk. Don't laugh.

There's someone on the other side of the vault door. I can hear the handle moving.

choices.choiceText: Is there a way to pin the door from your side?
Forget the door. Get to the vent now.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Light's off. I can't see a thing.

I'm wedged between a beam and the shelves. I can hear my own heartbeat, which is not helping.

choices.choiceText: Listen to me. Slow breaths. I'm right here.
Can you see any light under the door?

nodes.partnerDialogue: About eighty feet according to the old plans. There used to be a drainage structure down there. They claimed it was filled in, but the readings suggest part of it is still hollow.

choices.choiceText: That can be tomorrow's expedition. Tonight we get you out.
You really want to go back down there with me, don't you?

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Pretty much. And I'm getting static every time I touch the metal railing.

I hate admitting this, but I'm starting to think staying here any longer is a bad idea.

choices.choiceText: Then listen to that feeling. Into the vent, now.
Good. I need you alive more than I need another reading.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Okay. Ledger's in the dry bag. Vent cover is off.

I'm getting my pack through first. Don't hang up on me while I crawl in there.

choices.choiceText: I'm not going anywhere. Keep talking to me.
I'll meet you at the street exit. Tell me what you see when you're out.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
*paper rustles*

He wrote, 'We drilled until the bit struck bronze. The sound did not stop. It welcomed us.'

That's it. No explanation. Nothing after it.

choices.choiceText: Okay. Close the book. We leave now.
You can tell me the rest tomorrow. Right now I need you safe.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Crowbar, multitool, two contact mics, spare batteries, and a signal repeater.

I know. I overpack.

choices.choiceText: Tonight I'm very grateful that you overpack.
Good. Take the essentials and head for the vent.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I promise.

And... thank you. I know I joke about being fine all the time, but hearing you say 'don't do this alone' actually got to me.

choices.choiceText: Then don't. Let me stay on the line until you're outside.
You can lean on me a little, Evelyn.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
It's tight, but I can fit. I'm taking the jacket off and sending my bag ahead.

This is going to be deeply undignified.

choices.choiceText: I promise not to laugh. Probably.
Just keep moving. I'll be listening the whole way.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
*tiny laugh* Okay, okay. Lighter's away.

You're weirdly bossy when you're worried about me.

choices.choiceText: Only because you keep giving me reasons to worry.
Good. Now get into the duct before I start giving you a full safety lecture.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
The alley is behind the old water commission building on 6th. There's a rusted grate between two dumpsters.

If I lose signal, keep your headlights on. I should be able to see them through the rain.

choices.choiceText: I'll keep them on. Get out and come straight to the car.
And when you get in, you're getting the warmest seat and a coffee.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
*quiet exhale* You really remembered that.

Okay. I'm moving. And when I see your headlights, I'm probably going to have a very embarrassing emotional moment.

choices.choiceText: You can have your emotional moment. Just get to me safely.
I'll pretend I didn't see you cry if you pretend you didn't see me worrying.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
The next part says, 'Do not ventilate shaft nine.'

I don't know why, but after everything we've heard tonight, I'm not interested in finding out what fresh air is supposed to wake up.

choices.choiceText: Then we don't. Get out through the vent and leave it alone.
Agreed. We can investigate it another day, with actual backup.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Fifty-two. About as close to a resting heartbeat as I can reasonably call it.

I don't want to romanticize it, because I really don't know what it means. But I can't pretend it doesn't freak me out a little.

choices.choiceText: Then let it freak you out later. Right now, let's get you out.
We'll figure it out together when you're safe.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I got the contact mic down the crack. I'm recording a clean feed now.

And... okay. I got enough. I'm done tempting fate. I'm climbing out.

choices.choiceText: Good. Mission accomplished. Get moving.
You really just risked your life for one more recording.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Found it. I'm sliding the emergency pin through the striker now.

*heavy clunk*

Okay. That buys me a few minutes. I'm heading for the vent.

choices.choiceText: Good. Don't spend those minutes doing anything clever.
I'll stay quiet unless you need me. Keep moving.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
*breathes with you*

Okay. Better. The scraping stopped. I think whoever was out there moved on.

I hate that my first instinct was still to investigate it.

choices.choiceText: Save the detective work for daylight. Vent now.
That's one of the things I like about you. Even when you're scared, you're curious.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
There's a flashlight beam under the door. Twice. Then nothing.

I think it's just security doing rounds, but I'm not taking the chance. I'm moving while I can.

choices.choiceText: Go. I'm right here.
Text me when you're through the grate.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
You know what's funny? Ten minutes ago I'd have called going back down there 'an awful idea.'

Now I'm already thinking about what equipment we'd bring.

choices.choiceText: So there will be a next time. Good.
Only after coffee, daylight, and an actual safety plan.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
*metal scraping* I'm in the duct. This is the worst camping trip I've ever been on.

Wait... I can smell rain. I think I'm getting close.

choices.choiceText: Keep going. You're almost there.
You owe me a very boring coffee after this.
Talk to me. What do you see ahead?

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I'm near the exit. There's a rusted grate and a steam vent just past the brick substation.

Tell me you can actually see it from the street.

choices.choiceText: I see the steam. Keep coming toward me.
I'm parked where you can see the headlights. You're almost home.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
*iron grate clatters open; rain in the background*

I'm out. I'm actually out.

I see your headlights. Unlock the passenger door before I freeze out here, {PlayerName}.

choices.choiceText: Door's unlocked. Get in here, you idiot. You're soaked.
Come on. Warm car, dry towel, then you can tell me everything.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I checked that before calling you. The recorder's power cycle doesn't match it.

You're not wrong to ask, though. Honestly, I like that you challenge me when I get excited.

choices.choiceText: Then I'll keep asking questions. Someone has to keep you honest.
Good. Now let's focus on getting you home.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Wait... give me a second.

It's almost like someone trying to form a vowel and failing. There's a shape to it.

Okay, I officially hate this place.

choices.choiceText: Good. Hate it from somewhere safer. Get out.
You can hate it. I'll stay on the line until you're outside.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
*laughs softly* Climbing gear, extra batteries, two recorders, and you carrying the heavy case.

I'm already picturing it, which is probably a problem.

choices.choiceText: I'll carry the case. You handle the spooky science.
And afterward, we find somewhere warm and get breakfast.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
...Yeah. You're right.

I don't always notice when I've crossed that line until somebody else points it out. I get so focused on the answer that I forget there's a person attached to it.

Tonight that person needs to get home.

choices.choiceText: Exactly. The mystery can wait. You can't.
That's the version of you I want to know too.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Don't encourage me. Next time I'll bring a second bag just for batteries.

Although... having someone around who doesn't complain about the equipment would be nice.

choices.choiceText: I'll carry the batteries. You can carry the weird haunted gadgets.
Let's get you out first. Gear jokes later.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
That's the problem. I'm not very good at that.

But... maybe I can practice. Start with tonight.

choices.choiceText: Start with staying on the line with me.
Good. Then let me be useful for once.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
You better not laugh.

*pause*

Okay, you can laugh a little. This is objectively ridiculous.

choices.choiceText: I knew there was a funny side under all the field notes.
Now crawl, investigator.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
You know, that's actually kind of sweet.

Most people think the interesting part is the mystery. You're worried about whether I come home in one piece.

choices.choiceText: Because you matter more than the mystery.
Now stop distracting me and get through that vent.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Warm seat and coffee? You really did plan this.

Okay. That might be the nicest rescue I've ever had.

choices.choiceText: I'm trying to set a high standard.
Get in the car first. Flirting can wait until you're dry.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Deal.

And just so we're clear, I wasn't crying. My eyes were reacting to... rain. Aggressively.

choices.choiceText: Of course. Very scientific explanation.
Whatever helps you sleep tonight.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I like that.

Not 'I believe you no matter what,' just... 'we'll figure it out.' That feels better somehow.

choices.choiceText: You don't need blind belief. You need someone who stays curious with you.
And someone to pull you out of places like this.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I know.

You don't have to tell me twice. I do this every time. 'One more sample.' 'One more scan.' Then suddenly it's three in the morning and I'm eating crackers for dinner.

choices.choiceText: Then tonight you stop at one more sample.
I'll remind you to eat next time.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
That's probably the nicest way anyone has ever described it.

Most people just call me stubborn.

choices.choiceText: You can be stubborn and still be worth caring about.
Okay, enough emotional honesty. Get into the vent.

nodes.partnerDialogue: Deal. Rule one: we tell someone where we're going. Rule two: we bring two flashlights. Rule three... you don't disappear on me.

choices.choiceText: Rule three is easy.
Agreed. And rule four: breakfast after every investigation.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I would genuinely love that. No ghosts, no tunnels, no weird frequencies. Just coffee and something normal.

I think I need normal more than I realized.

choices.choiceText: Then we'll do boring. Very boring.
We'll earn the boring coffee first. Keep crawling.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I see a little gap ahead. There's streetlight coming through.

Oh my God... I can actually see the rain.

choices.choiceText: Almost there. Keep going.
I'm right outside. First thing you see is me.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I see them.

Okay. That feels weirdly comforting. I've been down here for what feels like hours, and suddenly seeing your headlights makes everything feel real again.

choices.choiceText: Come on. I'm getting you out of the rain.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Good. I actually want that.

Just don't get smug when you're right.

choices.choiceText: No promises.
I'll save the smugness for coffee.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Okay. Stay with me.

You know, I thought calling you from down here would make me feel more embarrassed. Instead it kind of feels like you're standing next to me.

choices.choiceText: Maybe that's exactly where I should be.
Then let's get you out and make that a real coffee date.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Okay, deal. I'll trust you with the heavy case.

Don't let that go to your head.

choices.choiceText: Too late.
I'll behave. Probably.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I have a funny side. It just gets buried under several layers of obsessive note-taking.

You might have to earn access to it.

choices.choiceText: I'll take that as a challenge.
Challenge accepted after we get you out.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
...You really know how to catch me off guard.

Okay. I needed to hear that tonight.

choices.choiceText: Then come home safe for me.
And maybe let me worry about you a little more often.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Yeah. I like that.

You don't have to understand everything I do. You just have to be willing to ask.

choices.choiceText: Then keep showing me your world.
First lesson: get out of the basement alive.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Please do. I'm terrible at noticing when I've skipped a meal.

And don't you dare tell anyone I admitted that.

choices.choiceText: Your secret is safe. Now move.
Deal. Coffee and food after this.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
...I know I'm not easy.

I think that's why this is getting to me. You're hearing the difficult parts and you're still here.

choices.choiceText: I'm still here.
Then get home and let me prove it over coffee.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Good. Because I'm starting to like having you around.

More than is probably sensible after one terrifying night underground.

choices.choiceText: You can decide what's sensible tomorrow.
Tonight we just get you home.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Breakfast after every investigation. I can live with that.

Pancakes, maybe. And no one is allowed to mention subsonic frequencies before I've eaten.

choices.choiceText: Deal. Pancakes first, paranormal theories later.
You're going to regret giving me permission to order pancakes for you.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I think I'd like that.

A quiet morning. Coffee. You. No abandoned buildings. No emergency exits. Just... normal.

choices.choiceText: Then that's what we're doing.
Let's start by getting you somewhere warm.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
That's a dangerous thing to say to someone who spends too much time alone.

I might actually start believing you.

choices.choiceText: Good. I mean it.
Then you'd better come out of that tunnel and test the theory.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I want that too.

Not just the investigations. The boring stuff. What you eat, what you do when you're tired, what makes you laugh. All of it.

choices.choiceText: Then we'll start with breakfast.
And I'll keep answering your weird questions too.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
*car door closes; rain becomes muffled*

Oh my God. Warmth. Dry seats. No concrete walls.

I think I forgot what normal air feels like.

choices.choiceText: Here. Towel first. Then breathe.
You made it. That's all I care about right now.
You look exhausted. Let me drive. No more investigating tonight.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
*quiet laugh* You're being very domestic for someone who just rescued me from a tunnel.

I like it.

choices.choiceText: Get used to it.
First we dry you off. Then you can tell me everything.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
I know.

And... thank you. I don't think I realized how scared I was until I got into this car and saw you sitting here.

choices.choiceText: You don't have to thank me. Just stay here with me for a minute.
Next time, maybe we do something that doesn't involve near-death experiences.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Yeah. I think I should let you.

My hands are still shaking a little.

choices.choiceText: Then let them shake. You're safe now.
Sit back. I'll get you somewhere warm.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
You're really still curious? After all that?

Okay. The short version is that the basement had something down there that matched the old recordings. The long version is going to take several coffees.

choices.choiceText: Then I'll buy the coffees.
I can live with that. Tell me the long version tomorrow.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
*soft laugh* Careful. I could get very comfortable with that.

Warm car. Rain outside. You sitting next to me. It feels... unexpectedly nice.

choices.choiceText: Then stay a little longer.
I'll take you home, but I'm not letting you disappear after tonight.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
...Okay. Just a minute.

No phones. No recordings. No case file.

Just us sitting here while the rain hits the windshield.

choices.choiceText: I could get used to this.
Me too, Evelyn.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
Then let's do something normal next time. Coffee. Breakfast. Somewhere with lights that actually work.

And you can make fun of how much equipment I carry.

choices.choiceText: Deal. And I'm choosing the breakfast place.
Deal. But I'm still hearing the full story eventually.

nodes.partnerDialogue: Okay. But you don't get to complain when I turn one coffee into a three-hour conversation about old recordings.

choices.choiceText: I think that's exactly what I'm signing up for.
Three hours? Fine. But pancakes are mandatory.

nodes.partnerDialogue:
...Tonight was terrifying. But hearing your voice through all of it made it easier.

I don't usually let people this close this quickly. I think you might be becoming an exception.

Get home safe, okay? And text me when you do. I'd like to wake up tomorrow and know you made it home too.
